digest.key_takeaway: Cloudflare has released Auto Router in public beta through AI Gateway, picking a model per request from a classifier that scores complexity, ambiguity, stakes and context dependence. Cloudflare’s own benchmark puts it ten points below Claude Opus 5.5 on success rate at a third of the cost, and practitioners have questioned how stakes survive a long agent session. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

articles.title: The focus on AI safety disasters ignores everyday harms
articles.summary: Consider what passes for success in technology policy. An AI company promises that its chatbot will not encourage suicide. A social media platform makes it more difficult for children to buy fentanyl. These are important protections, and they should have existed all along. But companies can clear these low bars while continuing to make products…

articles.title: Score Matching: Why Learning the Gradient of a Log-Density Beats Learning the Density Itself
articles.summary:
Score Matching: Why Learning the Gradient of a Log-Density Beats Learning the Density Itself


Most generative models try to learn a probability density. That sounds like the obvious goal, but it hides an awkward obstacle: the normalising constant. Score matching sidesteps it entirely by learning a different object, the gradient of the log-density, and that single change unlocks a family of models that includes modern diffusion models.

This article explains what the score is, why matching it is a sensible objective, how the practical estimators work, and where the idea breaks down.

articles.title: Taming Browser RAM Bloat: Building a Zero-Dependency LRU Eviction Daemon in Python
articles.summary:
If your workstation sounds like an aircraft carrier prepping for launch every time you research a technical problem, you aren't alone.

Modern web browsers are resource-hungry. Keeping 40+ tabs open across multiple windows easily chews through 6GB to 10GB of RAM. While browser extensions like OneTab or The Great Suspender exist, they run inside the browser process itself. When the browser’s render thread freezes under heavy load, extensions often choke alongside it.

articles.title: PyTorch Conference 2026: Google and Meta Open-Source TorchTPU for Native PyTorch on TPUs
articles.summary: Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google's TPUs, at PyTorch Conference North America 2026, and Meta said it plans to move larger LLM workloads onto TPUs with it. AWS released TorchNeuron for Trainium the same week, while developers questioned TPU availability and where vendor lock-in now sits. By Andrew Hoblitzell

articles.title: Google ML Drift Accelerates On-Device AI Inference Across Diverse GPUs
articles.summary: Google has released ML Drift, an open-source, cross-platform GPU compute engine designed for on-device AI and machine learning inference. Licensed under Apache 2.0, it abstracts the complexities of different GPU hardware and low-level APIs, supporting OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal, and WebGPU. By Sergio De Simone

articles.title: PHP Patches Two Critical RCE Flaws That Were Already Under Attack
articles.summary: PHP released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 to fix two critical vulnerabilities allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Amazon recorded an exploitation attempt four days before the patches shipped, and operators spent the day working out whether they ran PHP, where to get the package, and how to tell it had landed. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
